NAHHAS:v4p289/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p289/r20.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p289/r20.claim: Ibn Zayd explains يسرنا as بيّنا, “We made clear.”

NAHHAS:v4p289/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p289/r21.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p289/r21.claim: Mujahid explains يسرنا as هونا, “We made easy.”

NAHHAS:v4p289/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p289/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p289/r22.claim: The verse means God made the Qur'an easy through explanation and detail for anyone wishing to reflect and learn from it.
NAHHAS:v4p289/r22.anchor: ولقد سهلنا القرآن بتبييننا إياه وتفصيلنا لمن أراد أن يتذكره فيعتبر به

NAHHAS:v4p289/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p289/r23.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p289/r23.claim: Another explanation asks whether anyone seeks good or knowledge and is helped toward it; al-Nahhas says this is close to the first explanation, which better follows the verse's apparent sense.
NAHHAS:v4p289/r23.anchor: وقيل هل من طالب خيرا أو علما فيعان عليه فهذا قريب من الأول لأن الأول أبين على ظاهر الآية

SAMIN-DURR:54:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:17/r1.claim: يسرنا القرآن means “We prepared it for remembrance,” from يسر فرسه, preparing a horse for riding by bridling it; a poem uses ميسرا in this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:54:17/r1.anchor: هيأناه للذكر من قولهم: يسر فرسه، أي: هيأه للركوب بإلجامه.

ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r1.anchor: المعنى سهلنا، وقيل: إن كتب أهل الأديان نحو التوراة والإنجيل إنما يتلوها أهلها نظرا

ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r2.claim: One explanation contrasts the Quran with the Torah and Gospel: their adherents read those books by looking but rarely memorize them entirely as Muslims memorize the Quran.
ZAJJAJ:v5p88#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن كتب أهل الأديان نحو التوراة والإنجيل إنما يتلوها أهلها نظرا، ولا يكادون يحفظون كتبهم من أولها إلى آخرها كما يحفظ القرآن.

ASAD-NOTES:54:16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:54:16/r2.claim: God made the Qur'an easy to bear in mind and asks who will take it to heart.
ASAD-NOTES:54:16/r2.anchor: We made this Qur'an easy to bear in mind: [11]

ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r1.claim: Dhikr primarily means remembrance; Raghib defines it as something's presence in the mind, and here it joins understanding with remembering or bearing something in mind.

ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r2.claim: The same combined sense of understanding and remembering occurs in verses 22, 32 and 40 of this surah.
ASAD-NOTES:54:16#n11/r2.anchor: as used in the above context as well as in verses 22, 32 and 40

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r1.claim: The Noah narrative develops the question in 54:4: Quraysh should learn from earlier nations who rejected messengers and were punished, rather than follow their path toward doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r1.anchor: why they do not seek a lesson from the history of previous nations which has been narrated to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r2.claim: God's Book is a graciously revealed, fully equipped means for educating and instructing Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p84/r2.anchor: This Book is fully equipped with everything needed to educate and remind them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r1.claim: This reminder verse recurs after each prophetic story, so Islahi says its explanation need not be repeated at every occurrence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r1.anchor: This verse will be repeated after the end of every Prophetic anecdote

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r2.speaker: people generally
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r2.claim: People generally read the verse as saying the Qur'an is easy to memorize and consult for counsel; Islahi accepts this inference as correct but says the verse has wider scope.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r2.anchor: People have generally interpreted this verse to mean that the Almighty has made the Qur’ān a very easy book

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r3.claim: Taysīr means fitting something to its purpose and equipping it with the needed means; Islahi illustrates it as preparing a horse for riding and a person for a campaign.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r3.anchor: to make something appropriate for a specific objective and to embellish it with all the required means and needs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r4.speaker: Muḍarris ibn Rub‘ī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r4.claim: Muḍarris ibn Rub‘ī's cited poem describes helping a leader prepare for a campaign and equipping him to discharge leadership duties, witnessing this sense of taysīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r4.anchor: A poet, Muḍ arris ibn Rub‘ ī, belonging to the age of ignorance says

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r5.claim: Dhikr here covers educating, instructing, reminding, informing, warning, counseling, teaching a lesson, and conclusively communicating the truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r5.anchor: The meanings of educating and instructing the readers as well as reminding, informing, warning, counselling, teaching a lesson

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r6.claim: The Qur'an does not impose alien knowledge; it revives innate treasures of knowledge and understanding that people neglect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r6.anchor: does not impose something external on us; on the contrary, it revives and highlights the treasures of knowledge and cognizance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r7.claim: The reminder verse follows the earlier statement that the punishment warned of by the Prophet is inevitable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p88/r7.anchor: Earlier in the sūrah, it was said that the punishment which the Prophet (sws) was warning them of was inevitable

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r1.claim: The surrounding world and human nature, along with accounts of earlier nations, attest to punishment; deniers insist on seeing it, although the Qur’an already fully serves to educate and remind them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r1.anchor: This Qur’ān is fully equipped to fulfil this purpose.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r2.claim: Islahi rejects the idea that taysīr makes the Qur’an bland, only for recitation or memorization, or transparently understood by anyone with rudimentary Arabic; that misconception blocks reflection and access.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r2.anchor: every person who even has a vague and rudimentary knowledge of Arabic can fluently understand the Qur’ ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r3.claim: One aspect of taysīr is clear, eloquent Quraysh Arabic, neither garbled nor muddled, so Arabs could understand the message and had no excuse to deny God’s truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r3.anchor: It was set forth in the eloquent and articulate pure language of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r4.claim: Gradual revelation let the Prophet teach and recite the Qur’an over time so people could hear, understand, and absorb it; one instalment, as disbelievers demanded, would oppose taysīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r4.anchor: the Almighty revealed the Qur’ ān piecemeal so that the Prophet (sws) could gradually teach it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r5.claim: Basic teachings first came in concise, comprehensive verses and short surahs, aiding memorization, understanding, practice, and transmission; fuller explanation followed after people grew accustomed to the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p89/r5.anchor: all the basic teachings of the Qur’ ān were initially revealed in concise and succint verses and sentences

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r1.claim: A teaching repeated in varied styles, contexts, and backgrounds can be understood elsewhere when one presentation or argument is unclear; the Qur’an calls this variety taṣrīf.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r1.anchor: The Qur’ān has called this variety and diversity in its expression as taṣrīf

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r2.claim: Islahi describes seven groups of Makkan and Madinan surahs, with related yet distinct group contents; each surah has a counterpart whose paired discussion complements it, an arrangement made to facilitate taysīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p90/r2.anchor: Each sūrah has a counterpart and both members of a pair complement one another in the discussion of a topic.

QIRAAT-ER:54:17:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:54:17:5#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:54:17:5#1/r1.claim: The hmz form drops hamza, reading qurāna for qurʾāna through tashīl, in keeping with Ḥijāzī norms that lighten or elide hamza.
QIRAAT-ER:54:17:5#1/r1.anchor: Without hamza — reads qurāna instead of qurʾāna; the hamza is dropped (tashīl)

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r1.claim: The closing oath after each of four stories confirms the preceding warning that reports had come to them; each story alone warranted reflection and deterrence, yet they did not learn.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r1.anchor: جملة قسمية وردت في آخر القصص الأربع تقريرا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r2.claim: God made the Quran accessible by revealing it in the audience’s language, filling it with exhortation and examples, and alternating warning with promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r2.anchor: سهلنا القرآن لقومك بأن أنزلناه على لغتهم وشحناه بأنواع المواعظ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r3.claim: Here dhikr means taking heed and receiving admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r3.anchor: أي للتذكر والأتعاظ فهل من مدكر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r4.claim: The question emphatically denies the existence of anyone who takes heed: no respondent could answer yes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r4.anchor: فهل من مدكر إنكار ونفي للمتعظ على أبلغ وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r5.claim: Another view takes ‘made easy’ to mean easy to memorize, owing to its fine structure, eloquent wording, noble true meanings, and lack of obscure expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r5.anchor: وقيل : المعنى سهلنا القرآن للحفظ لما اشتمل عليه من حسن النظم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r6.claim: On the memorization reading, the question asks whether anyone seeks to memorize it so divine aid may support him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r6.anchor: فهل من طالب لحفظه ليعان عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr says no divine scripture besides the Quran has been memorized.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r7.anchor: قال ابن جبير : لم يستظهر شيء من الكتب الإلهية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the verse as God having made Quran recitation easy.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : يسرنا القرآن هونا قراءته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says that without God’s making it easy on human tongues, no creature could speak God’s speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس لو لا أن الله تعالى يسره على لسان الآدميين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r10.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r10.claim: Al-Daylami transmits a raised report from Anas making the same point about God enabling people to speak the Quran.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r11.speaker: ابن سيرين
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r11.claim: Ibn Sirin corrected someone who called a sura ‘light’: say ‘easy,’ following God’s description of the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذرعن ابن سيرين أنه مر برجل يقول سورة خفيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r12.claim: The admonition reading best fits the context; if authentic, the Anas report need not be an explanation of this verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r13.claim: Yassarnā may mean ‘prepared,’ as when one saddles a camel for travel or a horse for battle; the cited poetry witnesses this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p84/r13.anchor: وجوز ( يسرنا ) بهيأنا منقولهم : يسر ناقته للسفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r2.claim: God made the Qur’an easy so that people may remember and learn from it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r2.anchor: ولقد يسرنا} سهلنا {القرآن للذكر} ليتذكر ويعتبر به،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says it was made easy to memorize and recite; no other revealed book can be read in its entirety by heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: يسرناه للحفظ والقراءة، وليس شيء من كتب الله يقرأ كله ظاهرا إلا القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p429#2/r4.claim: The verse asks whether anyone will take heed from the Qur’an’s admonitions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r9.claim: God made the Quran easy or prepared it, as one prepares a camel for travel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r9.anchor: سهلناه أو هيأناه من يسر ناقته للسفر

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r10.claim: It is easy for admonition through varied lessons, or for memorization through concise and pleasant wording.
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:14-18/r10.anchor: للادكار والاتعاظ بأن صرفنا فيه أنواع المواعظ

BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r6.claim: The detailed stories were among the early Quranic material, made accessible to ease the community's learning.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r6.anchor: ولما كان هذا التفصيل مما أنزل أول القرآن تيسيرا على الأمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r7.claim: Facilitating the Quran for remembrance includes admonition, recollection, reflection, understanding, memorization, and honor for those who attend to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r7.anchor: أي الاتعاظ والتذكر والتدبر والفهم والحفظ والتشريف لمن يراعيه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r8.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r8.claim: Ibn Barrajān says the Arabic Quran was sent for understanding, addressed people in familiar ways, and taught them through examples.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r8.anchor: قال ابن برجان : أنزلناه باللسان العربي وأنزلناه للأفهام تنزيلا وخاطبناهم بعوائدهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r9.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r9.claim: Al-Qushayrī says recitation, knowledge, understanding, and memorization are made easy for different people, all of whom are the Quran's chosen people.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r9.anchor: وقال القشيري : يسر قراءته على ألسنة قوم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p351/r10.claim: God could have spoken in eloquent expressions no one understood, but instead used the most eloquent accessible language; this accessibility alongside unsurpassed eloquence is miraculous.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r1.claim: The Quran translates God's acts in the visible and unseen worlds and explains the divine names and attributes by which He makes Himself known.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r1.anchor: من أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا التي تعرف لنا بها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r2.claim: Human beings encompass traces of God's acts within themselves, enabling reflection on the Quran.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r2.anchor: فما من شيء من أفعاله إلا وفي نفسه منه أثر ظاهر ناظر للتفكر في القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r3.claim: Remembrance recalls what a person once knew but forgot and cannot summon independently until reminded.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r3.anchor: لما كان الإنسان يعرفه ثن نسيه حتى صار لا يستقل باستحضاره فإذا ذكر به ذكره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r4.claim: The closing question appeals to people to remember what God has made accessible for them to recall.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r4.anchor: فقال منبها على عظيم فعل العلم والقرآن الذي هو طريقه بالتكرار والتعبير

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r5.speaker: مطر الوراق
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r5.claim: Al-Bukhārī quotes Maṭar al-Warrāq glossing the question as asking whether there is a seeker of knowledge who will be helped.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r5.anchor: قال مطر الوراق : هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r6.claim: The reminder recurs four times in this surah; its final line appears separately from Quranic facilitation twice, at the Noah opening and after Pharaoh's story.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r6.anchor: وقد تكررت هذه الموعظة في هذه السورة أربع مرات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r7.claim: The phrase Which of your Lord's favors will you deny? recurs thirty-one times in al-Raḥmān.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r8.claim: The author speculates that the reminder alludes to five consecutive surahs and their endings; repeated letters, reversal, and assimilation point to the five senses as beginnings of knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r8.anchor: فكانت هذه الكلمة التي مدلولها الذكر مشيرة إلى الحواس الخمس الظاهرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r9.claim: He treats the first and last reminder clauses, omitting Quranic facilitation, as corresponding to two boundary letters assimilated into one and therefore to a single verse among the four.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p352/r9.anchor: وكان ما في أول هذه المواعظ وآخرها لخلوه عن ذكر القرآن موازيا للحرفين اللذين طرفهما للوهن بالتعبير والقلب لكن كان الحرفان بالإدغام كحرف واحد

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the Quran's being made easy for remembrance as making its recitation easy.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر} قال: هونا قراءته

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says no creature could speak God's speech if He had not made it easy on human tongues.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر} قال: لولا أن الله يسره على لسان الآدميين ما استطاع أحد من الخلق أن يتكلم بكلام الله

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r4.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet the same point that without God's facilitation no creature could speak His speech.

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r5.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r5.claim: Ibn Sirin says not to call a surah light; call it made easy, following this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r5.anchor: عن ابن سيرين أنه مر برجل يقول سورة خفيفة قال لا تقل سورة خفيفة ولكن قل سورة ميسرة

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the question as asking whether anyone will remember.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فهل من مدكر} قال: هل من متذكر

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab understands the question as asking whether anyone will be deterred from sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله {فهل من مدكر} قال: هل من منزجر عن المعاصي

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r8.claim: Qatada reads it as asking whether anyone seeks good and will be helped to attain it.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فهل من مدكر} قال: هل من طالب خير يعان عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r9.speaker: مطر الوراق
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r9.claim: Matar al-Warraq reads it as asking whether anyone seeks knowledge and will be helped to attain it.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r9.anchor: عن مطر الوراق في قوله {ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر} قال: هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p676/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r10.claim: Ibn Masud recited muthakkir with ذ, while the Prophet recited mudhakkir with د.
DURR-FULL:v7p676/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قرأت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم [فهل من مذكر] بالذال فقال {فهل من مدكر} بالدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r3.claim: مدكر derives from مذتذكر, an افتعل form of الذكر, meaning thought about evidence; the افتعال ت became د and ذ assimilated to د because their articulation points are close.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r3.anchor: أصله : مذتكر مفتعل من الذكر بضم الذال ، وهو التفكر في الدليل فقلبت تاء الافتعال دالا لتقارب مخرجيهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r4.claim: The reading of this verse is specifically transmitted from the Prophet; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to the related wording in Joseph 12:45.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r4.anchor: وقراءة هذه الآية مروية بخصوصها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتقدم في سورة يوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r8.claim: After warning through the Quran, God is praised for making it easy to grasp and use as guidance and admonition, while the polytheists deprive themselves by turning away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r8.anchor: لما كانت هذه النذارة بلغت بالقرآن والمشركون معرضون عن استماعه حارمين أنفسهم من فوائده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r9.claim: The Quran's ease signals God's care for it, as in the promise to preserve the Reminder; this encourages Muslims to study it and reproaches the polytheists in hope they relent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p186/r9.anchor: وهذا التيسير ينبىء بعناية الله به مثل قوله : { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r1.claim: God obliges Quran scholars to explain revelation explicitly, as 16:44 says, and implicitly, as the covenant in 3:187 says; this community is even more entitled to that duty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r1.anchor: فرض الله على علماء القرآن تبيينه تصريحا كقوله : { لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم } ( النحل : 44 ) ، وتعريضا كقوله : { وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r2.speaker: الحديث
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r2.claim: A hadith promises that people who gather in a mosque to recite and study God's Book receive tranquility and mercy, are surrounded by angels, and are remembered by God among those near Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( ما اجتمع قوم في بيت من بيوت الله يتلون كتاب الله ويتدارسونه بينهم إلا نزلت عليهم السكينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r3.claim: The lām attaches to يسرنا as a non-fixed adverbial and marks the beneficiary of the action, rather than a simple purpose or cause expressed by an object of reason.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r3.anchor: واللام في قوله : { للذكر } متعلقة ب { يسرنا } وهي ظرف لغو غير مستقر ، وهي لام تدل على أن الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r4.claim: This lām gives its object a special beneficiary relation, unlike the broader cause of a purpose-object; Ibn Hisham called it شبه التمليك, a label Ibn Malik followed in one work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r4.anchor: ابن هشام في ( مغني اللبيب ) : شبه التمليك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r5.speaker: ابن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r5.claim: Ibn Malik's label معنى التعدية, which Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers, captures that the lām's object behaves like an object of a transitive verb; it resembles the first object with كسا and أعطى.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r5.anchor: وأحسن من ذلك تسمية ابن مالك إياه في ( شرح كافيته ) وفي ( الخلاصة ) معنى التعدية . ولقد أجاد في ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p189/r6.claim: Examples of this beneficiary lām include God making spouses for people, granting Mary a guardian, and making livestock docile for people; ease for the easy or difficult path likewise names beneficiaries.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r1.claim: The basic meaning of the preposition lām is causation; other familiar uses began as metaphorical causal uses and became established enough for grammarians to treat them as separate meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r1.anchor: وأصل معاني لام الجر هو التعليل وتنشأ من استعمال اللام في التعليل المجازي معان شاعت فساوت الحقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r2.claim: Here الذكر means mental recollection rather than spoken mention: useful remembering that brings benefit and wards off harm, thus admonition and reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r2.anchor: والذكر : مصدر ذكر الذي هو التذكر العقلي لا اللساني ، والذي يرادفه الذكر بضم الذال اسما للمصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r3.claim: The phrase means Quranic guidance is made easy for the benefit of remembrance; swift reflection on hearing it is personified as a beneficiary, and يسرنا supplies the metaphor's imaginative image.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r3.anchor: ففي قوله : { يسرنا القرآن للذكر } استعارة مكنية ولفظ { يسرنا } تخييل . ويؤول المعنى إلى : يسرنا القرآن للمتذكرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r4.claim: This call to remember differs from the earlier one: the earlier reflection came from seeing traces of a ruined people, while this one comes from hearing, understanding, and following the Quran's exhortations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p190/r4.anchor: إلا أن بين الادكارين فرقا دقيقا ، فالادكار السالف ادكار اعتبار عن مشاهدة آثار الأمة البائدة ، والادكار المذكور هنا ادكار عن سماع مواعظ القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r8.claim: The form muddhakir derives from mudhtakir: tāʾ changes to dhāl to suit the following dāl, then the two dāls assimilate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r8.anchor: و: مدكر أصله: مذتكر، أبدلوا من التاء ذالا ليناسب الدال في النطق، ثم أدغموا الدال في الدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r9.claim: Abū Ḥātim says the common reading is transmitted from the Prophet with a sound chain; Qatāda's mudhakkir, assimilating the second consonant into the first, is poor because the same rule would alter other words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r9.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: رويت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإسناد صحيح وقرأ قتادة: «مذكر» بالذال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r12.claim: God made the Quran easy and accessible; dhikr here means memorizing it by heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r12.anchor: و: يسرنا القرآن معناه: سهلناه وقربناه و «الذكر» : الحفظ عن ظهر قلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r13.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr says that none of the other revealed books was memorized by heart, unlike the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r13.anchor: قال ابن جبير: لم يستظهر من كتب الله سوى القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r14.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r14.claim: Abū Muḥammad explains the Quran's ease through its excellent arrangement and noble meanings, which attract hearts and blend with sound minds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r14.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: يسر بما فيه من حسن النظم وشرف المعاني فله لوطة بالقلوب، وامتزاج بالعقول السليمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r15.claim: The question urges people to remember and memorize the Quran so its admonitions, knowledge, and guidance remain present in the mind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r15.anchor: استدعاء وحض على ذكره وحفظه لتكون زواجره وعلومه وهداياته حاضرة في النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r16.speaker: مطرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r16.claim: Muṭarrif understands the question as asking whether anyone seeks knowledge and will be helped in doing so.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215/r16.anchor: قال مطرف في قوله تعالى: فهل من مدكر هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.claim: The verse counts God's blessing in making guidance easy and expresses the hope that someone receives and follows it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: الآية تعديد نعمة في أن الله يسر الهدى ولا بخل من قبله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy for remembrance, meaning memorization and recitation, and the question urges people to remember and recite it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r1.anchor: أي سهلناه للذكر أي للحفظ والقراءة فهل من مدكر أي من ذاكر يذكره ويقرؤه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that, among the revealed books, only the Quran can be recited in its entirety by heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p94#3/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير ليس من كتب الله كتاب يقرأ كله ظاهرا إلا القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r2.claim: God made the Quran's wording easy and its meaning accessible to anyone who seeks it, so people may remember; 38:29 and 19:97 also describe reflection and ease in the Prophet's tongue.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r2.anchor: أي: سهلنا لفظه، ويسرنا معناه لمن أراده، ليتذكر الناس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r3.claim: Mujahid says God made Quran recitation easy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: {ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر} يعني: هونا قراءته.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Quran recitation was made easy on people's tongues.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: يسرنا تلاوته على الألسن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that without God's easing of Quran recitation on human tongues, no creature could speak God's words.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: لولا أن الله يسره على لسان الآدميين، ما استطاع أحد من الخلق أن يتكلم بكلام الله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir includes among this ease the Prophet's statement that the Quran was revealed according to seven ahruf, whose chains and wordings he discussed earlier.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478/r6.anchor: ومن تيسيره، تعالى، على الناس تلاوة القرآن ما تقدم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إن هذا القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r1.claim: The question asks whether anyone will remember through this Quran, whose memorization and meaning God made easy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فهل من مدكر} أي: فهل من متذكر بهذا القرآن الذي قد يسر الله حفظه ومعناه؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi reads the question as asking whether anyone will be deterred from sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: فهل من منزجر عن المعاصي؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r3.speaker: مطر الوراق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r3.claim: Matar al-Warraq explains it as asking whether a seeker of knowledge will be helped; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits it, al-Bukhari cites it with a definitive suspended attribution, Ibn Jarir also transmits it, and the same view is reported from Qatada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p478#2/r3.anchor: عن مطر -هو الوراق-في قوله تعالى: {فهل من مدكر} هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه؟

JISHUMI:v9p6681/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6681/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6681/r11.claim: مدكر derives from افتعل and remembrance: its original form مدتكر changes ta to dal to match the preceding dal, then assimilates the two dals.
JISHUMI:v9p6681/r11.anchor: قلبت التاء دالا لتؤاخي الدال بالميم

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy for reflection and recollection.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r1.anchor: للذكر لكي يتفكر فيه ويتذكر به

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains that the Quran was made easy to memorize and recite from memory, unlike other revealed books.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r2.anchor: ولا كتاب من كتب الله كذلك، عن سعيد بن جبير

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r3.claim: One who hears the warning is invited to take admonition.

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r4.speaker: قتادة ومطر الوراق
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r4.claim: Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq understand the question as asking whether anyone seeks knowledge and receives help in doing so.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r4.anchor: وقيل: هل من طالب علم، فيعان عليه، عن قتادة، ومطر الوراق

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r5.claim: The repeated question is not redundant: the first calls for reflection on the fates of the punished and saved, and the second for recalling the Quran's admonitions.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r5.anchor: أراد بالأول الاعتبار بأحوال المعذبين والناجين، وبالثاني التذكر بمواعظ القرآن

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r6.claim: These verses deter, frighten, and warn people lest the same fate that befell earlier peoples befall them.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r6.anchor: تدل الآيات على الزجر والتخويف والتحذير أن ينزل بهم مثل ما نزل بأولئك

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r8.claim: The Quran is sufficient for recollection, and its intended meaning can be known.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ولقد يسرنا القرآن) أنه شاف كاف في التذكر، وأنه يمكن معرفة المراد به

JISHUMI:v9p6684/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r9.claim: The question establishes that reflection is obligatory and that thinking is an act performed by people.
JISHUMI:v9p6684/r9.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فهل من مدكر) على وجوب التدبر، وأن التفكر فعلهم

BURSEVI:v9p224/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224/r7.claim: A mindful person should take the sign as a lesson, fear God, and abandon sin.
BURSEVI:v9p224/r7.anchor: أي معتبر بتلك الآية الحقيقة بالاعتبار فيخاف من الله ويترك المعصية

BURSEVI:v9p224/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224/r8.claim: The form derives from mudhtakir on the iftiʿāl pattern; its dhāl assimilated into tāʾ and became a doubled dāl.
BURSEVI:v9p224/r8.anchor: وأصله مذتكر على وزن مفتعل من الذكر فأدغمت الذال في التاء ثم قلبت دالا مشددة

BURSEVI:v9p224/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224/r10.claim: Bursevi identifies the closing statement about making the Quran easy as an oath-marked sentence.

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r1.claim: The repeated statement at the end of four narratives signals that each story alone should prompt recollection and restraint, though none was taken as a lesson.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r1.anchor: وردت في أواخر القصص الأربع تنبيها على أن كل قصة منها مستقبلة بإيجاب الأدكار كافية في الازدجار

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r2.claim: God made the Quran easy for the Prophet’s people by revealing it in their Arabic, enriching it with admonitions, and varying threats and promises.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r2.anchor: وبالله لبد سهلنا القرآن لقومك بأن أنزلنا على لغتهم كما قال فإنما يسرناه بلسانك

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r3.claim: “For remembrance” means for reminding and taking admonition.

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r4.speaker: الحسن عن النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r4.claim: Hasan reports from the Prophet that without God’s statement that the Quran was made easy for remembrance, tongues could not bear to speak it.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن عن النبي عليه السلام لولا قول الله ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر لما أطاقت الألسن

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r5.claim: The question rebukes and emphatically denies the existence of anyone who takes heed, phrased so strongly that nobody can answer yes.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r5.anchor: إنكار ونفي للمتعظ على أبلغ وجه وآكده حيث يدل على أنه لا يقدر أحد أن يجيب المستفهم بنعم

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud says he recited “mudhakkir” with dhāl, but the Prophet corrected it to “muddakir” with dāl.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r6.anchor: وعن عليه السلام بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : قرأت على النبي عليه السلام فهل من مذكر بالذال

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r8.claim: In the inward reading, Noah is the heart subdued by the commanding soul and human traits; God answers his plea, lets luminous spiritual qualities overcome animal darkness, and saves him on their ship while destroying the lower self.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r8.anchor: وفي الآيات إشارة إلى مغلوبية نوح القلب في يد النفس الأمارة بغلبات الصفات البشرية عليه حتى دعا ربه فأجابه الله

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r9.claim: The Flood’s heavenly waters signify compassion, mercy, and generosity from the world of spirits, while springs from human earth signify knowledge and realities.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r9.anchor: وأفاض من سماء الأرواح العلوية مياه الرأفة والرحمة والكرامة ومن أرض البشرية عيون المعارف والحقائق

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r10.claim: When unveiling and direct vision increase, spirits yearn for annihilation; God carries them in ships of protection, guided by providential care.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r10.anchor: إذا زاد الكشف والعيان تستشرف الأرواح على الفناء فيدخلها الله في سفن الصعمة ويجريها بشمال العناية

BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r11.claim: Prophets and saints are ships of divine care: those who follow their way escape error and misery and enter the Merciful’s protection.
BURSEVI:v9p224#2/r11.anchor: أن الأنبياء والأولياء سفن عنايته تعالى يتخلص العباد بهم من الاستغراق في بحار الضلالة وظلمات الشقاوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r25.claim: Making the Quran easy for remembrance means making its recitation accessible to speakers of every language; al-Mawardi calls this one of its miracles.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r25.anchor: لأن الأعجمي قد يقرأه ويتلوه كالعربي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r26.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r26.claim: Maqatil explains the phrase as making the Quran's knowledge and the derivation of its meanings easy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r26.anchor: سهلنا علم ما فيه واستنباط معانيه ، قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r27.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p411#2/r27.claim: Al-Farra says God made the Quran easy to memorize, making it the easiest book to retain.

MUJAHID:v2p636#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p636#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p636#4/r1.claim: Mujahid explains that God made the Quran's recitation easy.
MUJAHID:v2p636#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر ﴾ قال هونا قراءته

MUQATIL:54:15-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:54:15-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:54:15-18/r3.claim: God made the Quran easy for remembrance; without that ease no one could speak God's words, but he enabled people to recite it in all circumstances.
MUQATIL:54:15-18/r3.anchor: يقول: هونا { القرآن للذكر } يعني ليتذكروا فيه { فهل من مدكر } [آية: 17] يعني فيتذكر فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r25.claim: God made the Quran easy to memorize and helps anyone who seeks to memorize it; the question invites a learner to seek that help.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r25.anchor: أي سهلناه للحفظ وأعنا عليه من أراد حفظه

QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r26.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r26.claim: Alternatively, yassarnā means preparing the Quran for remembrance, by analogy with saddling a mount or horse.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r26.anchor: ولقد هيأناه للذكر مأخوذ من يسر ناقته للسفر

QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r27.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r27.claim: The cited line depicts a horse prepared for war by saddling and bridling it.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:13-17/r27.anchor: ويسر فرسه للغزو إذا أسرجه وألجمه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r1.claim: The verse can mean God prepared the Quran for remembrance, like preparing a mount or horse; the accompanying poetry uses mayssiran for a bridled horse.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r1.anchor:
وقمت إليه باللجام ميسرا
هنالك يجزيني الذي كنت أصنع

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says no revealed book besides the Quran can be recited entirely from memory.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ليس من كتب الله كتاب يقرأ كله ظاهرا إلا القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r3.claim: Another account says Israelites read the Torah from a written copy except Moses, Aaron, Joshua, and Ezra; they marveled when Ezra rewrote it from memory after it burned.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: ولم يكن هذا لبني إسرائيل، ولم يكونوا يقرؤون التوراة إلا نظرا

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r4.claim: God eased preservation of His Book for this community so remembrance can take root in them until it becomes like an innate trait.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r4.anchor: فيسر الله تعالى على هذه الأمة حفظ كتابه ليذكروا ما فيه أي يفتعلوا الذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r5.claim: Here the question asks whether anyone will recite the Quran.

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وابن شوذب
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r6.claim: They take the question to invite anyone seeking good and knowledge, who will then receive help.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وابن شوذب: فهل من طالب خير وعلم فيعان عليه،

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r7.claim: The verse is repeated in this surah to draw attention and make the message understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r7.anchor: وكرر في هذه السورة للتنبيه والإفهام.

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r8.claim: Another explanation says each story of past peoples and messengers is itself a reminder, so the question recurs after each account.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r8.anchor: ما عاملتهم به الأمم، وما كان من عقبى أمورهم

QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r9.claim: The particle hal summons listeners’ implanted understanding as evidence against them; the text assigns the lam to calling forth and haʾ to eliciting.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:15-17/r9.anchor: تستدعي أفهامهم التي ركبت في أجوافهم وجعلها حجة عليهم

QASHANI:54:15-17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:54:15-17/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:54:15-17/r2.claim: The call asks whether anyone will take admonition, since the path of truth is one and all prophets agree on the foundations of revealed laws.
QASHANI:54:15-17/r2.anchor: متعظ، فإن طريق الحق واحد والأنبياء كلهم متوافقون في أصول الشرائع

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r1.claim: The positive refrain follows an ominous refrain: the first stresses wrath for rejecting God and signs, the second mercy through easy access to revelation and truth.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r1.anchor: The first refrain emphasizes the wrath that comes upon those who reject God and His signs, while the second emphasizes the mercy

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r2.claim: Making the Quran easy to remember is mercy: recitation is easy for the tongue, and understanding and memorization for mind and heart.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r2.anchor: its recitation is made easy for the tongue and the understanding and memorization of it are made easy for the mind and heart (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r3.claim: One hadith praises those who learn the Quran and teach it to others as the best among people.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r3.anchor: The best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it to others

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r4.claim: Another hadith says God will never burn in Hell someone who has memorized the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r4.anchor: If the Quran is enclosed by skin [i.e., memorized by a human being], God will never burn it in Hellfire

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r5.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r5.claim: Remember may mean be admonished, and the question may ask who will take admonition or heed.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r5.anchor: could also be understood to mean, “to be admonished” (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:54:17/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r6.claim: Either sense can allude to the pretemporal covenant, asking who remembers or heeds the pact with God.
STUDYQURAN:54:17/r6.anchor: it can also be understood as a reference to the covenant made between God and human beings before time (see 7:172c)

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r2.claim: The account of Noah is given with the most eloquent expression, the fewest words, and the fullest meaning.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r2.anchor: أفصح بيان وأقصر كلام وأتم معنى

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r3.claim: Noah lived longer than the other prophets and endured affliction more intensely than they did.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r3.anchor: وكان نوح - عليه السلام - أطول الأنبياء عمرا ، وأشدهم للبلاء مقاساة

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r4.claim: After Noah's people perished, God preserved Noah and his children; the people of the earth descend from Noah's children.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r4.anchor: لما نجى نوحا متعه بعد هلاك قومه ومتع أولاده ، فكل من على وجه الأرض من أولا د نوح عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r5.claim: The story gives religious people hope: God soon destroys their enemies, enables them to possess their lands, and grants victory to His allies, as with Moses and Pharaoh.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r5.anchor: فإن الله يهلك - عن قريب - عدوهم ، ويمكنهم من ديارهم وبلادهم ، ويورثهم ما كان إليهم . وكذلك كانت قصة موسى عليه السلام مع فرعون وقومه

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r6.claim: God makes Qur'an recitation easy on tongues and its knowledge, understanding, and memorization easy in the hearts of different groups; all are people of the Qur'an and God's elect.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r6.anchor: يسرنا قراءته على ألسنة الناس ، ويسرنا علمه على قلوب قوم ، ويسرنا فهمه على قلوب قوم ، ويسرنا حفظه على قلوب قوم

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r7.claim: A Sufi saying describes God communicating through the Qur'an with some spirits before they entered bodies, and asks whether anyone will remember that covenant.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r7.anchor: ويقال : كاشف الأرواح من قوم - بالقرآن - قبل إدخالها في الأجساد . { فهل من مدكر } لهذا العهد الذي جرى لنا معه

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r8.claim: The verse also means that recitation and memorization have been made easy; no other revealed book is memorized in its entirety like the Qur'an.
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r8.anchor: هونا قراءته وحفظه ؛ فليس كتاب من كتب الله تعالى يقرأ ظهرا إلا القرآن

QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p258/r12.claim: The repeated refrain stresses that God made Qur'an recitation and memorization easy.

TAB-FULL:v22p131/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r1.claim: God made the Quran easy, explained and distinguished it for anyone who wishes to remember, reflect, and take admonition.
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {يسرنا القرآن للذكر} [القمر: 40] قال: «هوناه»

TAB-FULL:v22p131/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses God's making the Quran easy as making it manageable.
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {يسرنا القرآن للذكر} [القمر: 40] قال: «هوناه»

TAB-FULL:v22p131/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as making the Quran clear.
TAB-FULL:v22p131/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر} [القمر: 40] قال: " يسرنا: بينا "

SULAMI:v2p290#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p290#6/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p290#6/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says the Qur'an is made easy for the one who remembers and whose heart is taught by its spirit; the verse asks who will remember what God has already brought to them.
SULAMI:v2p290#6/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : يسر القرآن لمن ذكره وعلم روحه قلبه فهل من مدكر أي هل من ذاكر

TUSTARI:54:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:54:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:54:17/r1.claim: God made the Qur'an easy for remembrance; without that ease, tongues could not bear to speak it, so people should take heed of this gift.
TUSTARI:54:17/r1.anchor: هونا القرآن للذكر، ولولا ذلك لما أطاقت الألسنة

TABATABAI:54:16-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:16-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:16-18/r4.claim: The repeated reminder that the Qur’an is made easy for remembrance states the aim of the warning and admonition.
TABATABAI:54:16-18/r4.anchor: ثم ثناه بذكر الغرض من الإنذار والتخويف

TABATABAI:54:16-18#2/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:16-18#2/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:16-18#2/r17.claim: Making the Qur’an easy for remembrance means expressing its purposes so people of simple or deep understanding can grasp them according to their capacity.
TABATABAI:54:16-18#2/r17.anchor: التيسير التسهيل وتيسير القرآن للذكر هو إلقاؤه على نحو يسهل فهم مقاصده للعامي والخاصي والأفهام البسيطة والمتعمقة كل على مقدار فهمه

TABRISI:54:14-18/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:14-18/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:14-18/r19.claim: God made the Quran easy to memorize and recite; its clear expression, evident proofs, sound rulings, and true meanings make learning accessible and encourage people to gain knowledge.
TABRISI:54:14-18/r19.anchor: سهلناه للحفظ والقراءة حتى يقرأ كله ظاهرا

TABRISI:54:14-18/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:14-18/r20.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:54:14-18/r20.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the Quran is the only revealed book that can be recited entirely from memory.
TABRISI:54:14-18/r20.anchor: إلا القرآن عن سعيد بن جبير والتيسير للشيء هو تسهيله

TABRISI:54:14-18/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:14-18/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:14-18/r21.claim: Making a path to knowledge easy is a strong reason to pursue it and gain a great share of learning.
TABRISI:54:14-18/r21.anchor: فمن سهل له طريق العلم فهو حقيق بأخذ الحظ الجزيل منه

TABRISI:54:14-18/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:14-18/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:14-18/r22.claim: Remembrance leads to knowledge: someone heedless of a thing or its proof cannot know it while heedless, but recalling the evidence and its paths opens knowledge in its proper way.
TABRISI:54:14-18/r22.anchor: لأن الساهي عن الشيء أو عن دليله لا يجوز أن يعلمه في حال سهوه

TABRISI:54:14-18/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:14-18/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:14-18/r23.claim: The repeated question urges people to take heed, reflect, and consider the Quran.
TABRISI:54:14-18/r23.anchor: أي متعظ معتبر به ناظر فيه

FARRA:v3p107/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p107/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p107/r1.claim: God made the Qur’an easy to speak; without that, people could not manage speech from God.
FARRA:v3p107/r1.anchor: وقوله: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر (17) . يقول : هوناه ولولا ذلك ما أطاق العباد أن يتكلموا بكلام الله.

FARRA:v3p107/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p107/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p107/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God made it easy to memorize; no other book is memorized completely by heart.
FARRA:v3p107/r2.anchor: ويقال : ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر: للحفظ، فليس من كتاب بحفظ ظاهرا غيره.

THALABI:v9p165/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p165/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p165/r2.claim: God made the Quran easy and accessible for people to remember, take warning from, and reflect on.
THALABI:v9p165/r2.anchor: ولقد يسرنا سهلنا وهونا القرآن للذكر اي ليتذكر ويعتبر به ويتفكر فيه،

THALABI:v9p165/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p165/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v9p165/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Quran was made easy to memorize by heart, and no other revealed book can be recited entirely from memory.
THALABI:v9p165/r3.anchor: وليس من كتب الله كتابا يقرأ كله ظاهرا إلا القرآن.

THALABI:v9p165/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p165/r4.speaker: مطر الوراق
THALABI:v9p165/r4.claim: Maṭar al-Warrāq takes the question to ask whether any seeker of knowledge is there who will be helped.
THALABI:v9p165/r4.anchor: عن مطر الوراق في قول الله سبحانه فهل من مدكر قال: هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه.

THALABI:v9p165/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p165/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p165/r5.claim: The phrase asks whether anyone will take admonition from the Quran's exhortations.

THALABI:v9p168/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p168/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p168/r10.claim: God made the Quran easy for people, so that they may remember it.
THALABI:v9p168/r10.anchor: ولقد يسرنا هونا عليهم القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r3.claim: Muqatil glosses the question as asking whether anyone will remember that the warning is true, learn from it, and fear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: فهل من متذكر يعلم أن ذلك حق فيعتبر ويخاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r4.claim: The underlying form is mudh-takir; tāʾ changes to dāl and dhāl assimilates into dāl, since the voiced dāl better matches the voiced sound than the voiceless tāʾ; compare muzdajir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r4.anchor: وأصله مذتكر، ولكن التاء أبدل منها الدال، والذال من موضع التاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي عن سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r5.claim: Abu Ali cites Sibawayh for a form with dhāl in al-dhikr, supported by a verse of Ibn Muqbil.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r6.claim: The high frequency of the dāl forms ادكر and مدكر made the root resemble patterns such as taqwā, taqiya, and taqāt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p101/r6.anchor: لما كثر تصرف الكلمة بالدال نحو ادكر، وهل من مدكر أشبهت تقوى وتقية وتقاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r1.claim: One interpretation takes dhikr as memorization and recitation; the Qur'an is the only revealed book people recite entirely from memory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن المراد بالذكر هاهنا الحفظ والقراءة، وهو قول سعيد بن جبير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says that without God's making the Qur'an easy, no one could speak God's words; God made it accessible to creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لولا أن الله يسر القرآن ما استطاع أحد أن يتكلم بكلام الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj observes that followers of other religions generally read the Torah and Gospel from a text and rarely memorize them entirely as Muslims memorize the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: قيل: إن كتب أهل الأديان نحو التوراة والإنجيل إنما يتلوها أهلها نظرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r4.claim: On the recitation reading, the question urges people to recite, study, learn, and understand the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى قوله {فهل من مدكر} أي هل من ذاكر يذكره، وقارئ يقرأه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r5.speaker: مطر الوراق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r5.claim: Matar al-Warraq paraphrases the question as asking whether there is a seeker of knowledge who will be helped.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مطر الوراق: هل من طالب علم فيعان عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r6.claim: A second interpretation takes dhikr to mean reflection and taking heed of what the Qur'an contains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r6.anchor: القول الثاني: أن معنى الذكر هاهنا الاعتبار والتفكر، قال مقاتل: يعني ليتذكروا ما فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r7.claim: God made the Qur'an easy by giving it clear, understandable rather than difficult wording and by setting out admonitions and warnings, as in 26:195.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p102#2/r7.anchor: هوناه بأن جعلنا ألفاظه سهلة مفهومة لا صعبة متعقدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r1.claim: On the reflection reading, the question asks whether anyone will take admonition, reflect, and fear.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r2.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God made the Qur'an easy for anyone willing to take admonition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p103/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال: يريد سهلنا القرآن لكل متعظ

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p432#3/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p432#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p432#3/r7.claim: God made the Quran easy to recite; otherwise people could neither articulate it nor listen to it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p432#3/r7.anchor: أي سهلناه للتلاوة. ولولا ذلك: ما أطاق العباد أن يلفظوا به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r9.claim: God made the Quran easy to memorize; no other revealed book is memorized by heart in this way.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r9.anchor: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر } سهلناه للحفظ، فليس يحفظ كتاب من كتب الله ظاهرا إلا القرآن { فهل من مدكر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:12-17/r10.claim: The question calls for someone to take admonition from the Quran's teachings.

ELMALILI:54:9-17/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r16.claim: Muddakkir derives from muztakir on iftiʿāl from dhikr; tā changes to dāl and dhāl assimilates into dāl.
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r16.anchor: olduğu gibi tâ, dâl’e kalb olunmuş, sonra da zâl dâl’de idgam edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:54:9-17/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r19.claim: God made the Qur’an easy or readily granted so that people would reflect.
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r19.anchor: Şânım nâmına Kur’ân’ı da müyesser kıldık, kolaylaştırdık, yahut kolaylıkla ihsan eyledik

ELMALILI:54:9-17/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r20.claim: The refrain follows each story, recalling previous reports as deterrence and making each narrative a distinct call to reflect.
ELMALILI:54:9-17/r20.anchor: bu sûrenin bir tercî‘âyetidir ki her kıssanın akabinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r8.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r8.claim: The recurring refrain in verses 22, 32, 40, and 17 presents the Qur'an as a book for reflection and admonition; examples of past peoples sharpen its light, and the audience's indifference is rebuked.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r8.anchor: muhataplarınca gösterilen duyarsızlığa vurgu yapılıp bu tutum kınanmaktadır (Zemahşerî, IV, 46).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r9.claim: Muddakkir, rendered as one who reflects, can also mean someone who takes a lesson, admonition, or instruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r9.anchor: Bu âyetteki “düşünecek” diye çevrilen müddekir kelimesini “ibret alan, öğüt alan, ders çıkaran” şeklinde de tercüme etmek mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r10.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r10.claim: Tabari also explains the question as asking whether anyone wants what is good so that they may be helped.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r10.anchor: “Düşünecek yok mu?” cümlesi, “Hayırlı olanı isteyen var mı ki yardım edilsin!” mânasıyla da açıklanmıştır (Taberî, XXVII, 96-97).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r11.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r11.claim: The phrase about making the Qur'an easy has also prompted discussion of its distinctive expression and the ease of understanding and memorizing it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:9/r11.anchor: Kur’an’ın kendine özgü ifade özellikleri, anlaşılma ve ezberlenmesinin kolay oluşu gibi hususlar üzerinde durulmuştur (meselâ bk. İbn Âşûr, XXVII, 187-190).

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشرى
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the Qur'an was made easy for recollection and admonition by interweaving healing admonitions and varying promise and threat.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r7.anchor: قال في الكشاف 2 أي سهلناه للادكار والاتعاظ بأن نسجناه 3 بالمواعظ الشافية

ITQAN:v3p180/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p180/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p180/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the al-Qamar refrain renews admonition at each story, since every report deserves its own reflection and should awaken listeners from heedlessness.
ITQAN:v3p180/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري كرر ليجددوا عند سماع كل نبأ منها إتعاظا وتنبيها وإن كلا من تلك الأنباء مستحق لإعتبار يختص به

ITQAN:v3p180/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p180/r7.speaker: صاحب عروس الأفراح
ITQAN:v3p180/r7.claim: The author of ʿArus al-Afrah answers that these repetitions are not verbosity when each wording intends a different preceding event.
ITQAN:v3p180/r7.anchor: قال في عروس الأفراح فإن قلت إذا كان المراد بكل ما قبله فليس ذلك بإطناب بل هي ألفاظ كل أريد به غير ما أريد بالآخر

DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.claim: Yusr and taysīr mean facilitation or making something easy, including the Qur'an and God's provision of an easy outcome.
DAMGHANI:v1p502/r9.anchor: الخامس اليسر والتيسير التسهيل قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r5.claim: The refrain هل من مدكر means, “Is there anyone who will take heed and be admonished?”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r5.anchor: ومثل ذلك تكرار فهل من مدكر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p6/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p6/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p6/r1.claim: The Quran's inimitability exceeds description; when a heart is receptive, its reminders awaken awe, tears, and a felt recognition of divine speech, whereas a closed heart cannot yet grasp what he describes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p6/r1.anchor: فعند ذاك تذوق ما لم تعهد له مذاقاً ولا طعماً وتحسّ ما لم يكن لك فيه سابق معرفة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r3.claim: The repeated refrain interrupts the arguments to challenge the stubborn audience to reflect on the truth established by sound proofs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r3.anchor: Such repetitive verses in a sūrah occupy a special significance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p78/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p78/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p78/r3.claim: The Qur’an is a blessing that warns in advance and makes it easy for the Quraysh to take heed and remember.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p78/r3.anchor: He has made it easy for them so they can seek a lesson from it and be reminded.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r3.claim: God made the Qur'an easy for admonition and reflection because it contains admonition, promise, and threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r3.anchor: ولقد يسرنا: أي سهلنا، القرآن للذكر: أي للإذكار والاتعاظ، لما تضمنه من الوعظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses مدكر as someone who takes admonition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: من متعظ. وقال قتادة: فهل من طالب خير؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses مدكر as someone seeking good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: من متعظ. وقال قتادة: فهل من طالب خير؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb glosses مدكر as someone deterred from sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: فهل من مزدجر عن المعاصي؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r7.claim: Another view takes remembrance to mean memorization, made easy by the Qur'an's fine ordering, sound wording, lack of filler, and honorable, true meanings that engage hearts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: للذكر: للحفظ، أي سهلناه للحفظ، لما اشتمل عليه من حسن النظم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r8.claim: Under the memorization view, the verse asks whether anyone seeks to memorize it and receive help, keeping its admonitions and teachings present in mind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r8.anchor: فهل من مدكر: أي من طالب لحفظه ليعان عليه، وتكون زواجره وعلومه حاضرة في النفس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r9.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jubayr says none of the revealed books besides the Qur'an has been memorized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: لم يستظهر شيء من الكتب الإلهية غير القرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r10.claim: A further gloss takes يسرنا as prepared the Qur'an for remembrance, like preparing a camel for travel or a horse for war.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: يسرنا: هيأنا القرآن للذكر، كقولهم: يسر ناقته للسفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r11.claim: The cited poem uses ميسرا for a horse prepared with its bridle, illustrating the sense of equipping or preparing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p40#2/r11.anchor: وقمت إليه باللجام ميسرا ... هنالك يجزيني الذي كنت أصنع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r5.claim: The repeated refrain says the Qur'an is accessible for remembrance, removing the excuse that its warnings and lessons are too difficult to understand.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r5.anchor: ولقد سيرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r6.claim: Believers need to accept all revelation and act on its clear rulings; deeper understanding of difficult and ambiguous matters is a gift God grants to people He elevates in knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r6.anchor: يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r7.claim: Repeated accounts of prophets and their peoples across several sūras provide sufficient lessons, while combining them yields a straight path and manifest light.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p342/r7.anchor: تكرار قصص الأنبياء مع أممهم في عدة سور
